charts.subtitle: Current vectorized-recipe runs; collected throughput uses rollout seconds, while total time remains available in tooltips.

charts.title: Final-recipe throughput across seeds
charts.subtitle: Warm sequential and vectorized runs across three seeds; collected throughput is rollout-only.

charts.rationale: Three discrete seed measurements are clearer as bars than as an underpowered distribution plot.

charts.title: Final-recipe wall-time composition
charts.subtitle: Rollout, preparation, and update seconds for current vectorized-recipe runs, plus legacy final rows.
charts.question: Where is final-recipe training time spent?
charts.rationale: Stacked bars compare total wall time and its mutually exclusive phases.

tables.subtitle: Each row remains a separate source run; repeated pairs are not silently pooled.

tables.subtitle: Exact normalized metrics; blank cells were not reported or cannot be derived safely.

tables.subtitle: Observed safeguards are not promoted to pass/fail without an explicit source verdict.

blocks.body:
## Champion and time-to-beat

No current input explicitly designates a champion, so the dashboard does not turn the descriptive Bradley–Terry leader into a champion. A time-to-beat is reported only when future normalized data marks both champion and candidate roles and the candidate's 95% confidence interval is entirely above 50%.

## Tournament evidence

Point estimates, Wilson intervals, observed cross-play, schedule-aware ratings, and seat effects are shown only for source-backed tournament rows.

## Learning curves

**No data.** Current inputs contain aggregate speed and tournament results, not checkpoint metrics indexed by wall time or environment decisions. The normalized schema includes `learning_curve` for future runs.

## Training throughput and time

Current vectorized runs separate rollout collection throughput from end-to-end throughput and report environment turns. The legacy file's samples map to collected policy decisions, while its environment turns remain blank. Baseline and interim caveats remain visible in detail.

## Resources

**Partial data.** Vectorized runs report RSS peaks and CUDA allocation peaks; the original CUDA baseline also reports a CUDA peak. CPU/GPU utilization and utilization time series are absent, so no utilization chart is rendered.

## Correctness and information safety

Source-described ratio checks and smoke-test configuration checks are preserved with their original verdict strength. No illegal-action result or complete benchmark-level information-leakage result is present; absence is not a pass.

## Reproducibility and provenance

Every normalized row records its source path and SHA-256. Checkpoint hashes, recipes, seeds, hardware, observation versions, and benchmark git SHAs remain explicitly missing when the source does not supply them.
